study type: Prospective observational study with historical control
exposure: 30 s delay of umbilical cord clamping
outcome: Respiratory distress at 1 and 6 hours after birth
cohort: 64 infants born after elective CS and 334 infants born vaginally (166 early clamped and 168 delayed clamped) at a Swedish county hospital
finding: Infants born by elective CS with a 30-second cord clamping delay had higher iron stores at 4 months of age compared to those born vaginally with early cord clamping, and comparable iron status to those with 180-second delayed cord clamping after vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Waiting 30 seconds to clamp the umbilical cord after elective CS results in higher iron stores at 4 months of age compared with early cord clamping after vaginal birth.
